title: National Printing Press workers strike over unpaid pay and conditions
organizer: National Printing Press workers; formal organizer not reported
participants_original: No workforce or assembly count reported.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened report says workers began a strike, but gives no turnout and does not describe a public gathering; a group of 50 or more is not established.

start_date.summary: The 6 January report says the strike began on the preceding Wednesday; 4 January is the direct calendar conversion.

location.summary: The report places the National Printing Press workers’ strike in Yaoundé.

organizer.summary: The article identifies National Printing Press workers but no formal union or organizer.

demands.summary: Workers demanded unpaid salaries and bonuses, improved conditions, and the director general’s departure.

participants_original.summary: The article does not estimate how many workers joined the strike or assembled.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No participant count or physical public assembly is described.

state_target.summary: The strike is framed as an employer wage and conditions dispute; workers planned to approach competent authorities including the Communication Ministry, but the report does not establish a demand directed to state policy or the employer’s ownership.

end_date.summary: The article reports the strike’s start but no physical end or final day.

protester_violence.summary: The report does not describe violence by workers; the field remains unknown.

state_response.summary: No state response to the strike is established. The director general’s explanation about blocked treasury disbursements is not coded as a state response.

notes: The date 4 January is inferred from the 6 January article’s “preceding Wednesday.” This is a reported strike, not a verified public assembly. Do not treat intended ministry contact as an executed state-directed demand; state ownership and direct state target remain open.
open_questions: Did 50 or more people assemble during the strike?
Was the employer a state body and was any demand directed to government action?
When did the strike physically end?
Was any state response specifically tied to this strike?

title: BLT/SOCOPAO workers gather over severance and labor-rights dispute
location: Unknown; the report does not locate the 20 January gathering
organizer: A collective of BLT Cameroun and SOCOPAO Cameroun workers; formal organizer not named
participants_original: The article reports about 800 workers concerned by the dispute, but gives no count for the 20 January gathering.
threshold_50_evidence: The report says workers gathered to amend a strike notice but gives no attendance count. The 800 workers concerned by the dispute are not the assembly count.

start_date.summary: The article dated 21 January says a worker collective met on 20 January to amend a strike notice.

location.summary: The 20 January gathering’s site is not reported. A separate 18 January tripartite meeting took place at the Labor Delegation in Douala.

organizer.summary: The report attributes the gathering to a collective of BLT/SOCOPAO workers; it does not name a union or formal organizer.

demands.summary: The dispute concerns severance, indemnities and labor rights owed by the private Bolloré group.

participants_original.summary: About 800 employees were affected by the dispute, but no number is given for those who gathered on 20 January.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No attendance estimate is attached to the 20 January gathering; do not substitute the 800 affected employees.

state_target.summary: The article urges the labor minister to help resolve a dispute primarily with a private employer. Whether the gathering directed a demand to the Cameroonian state remains uncertain.

end_date.summary: No duration or physical end of the 20 January gathering is given.

protester_violence.summary: The account does not report violence by participants; the field remains unknown.

state_response.summary: A failed tripartite labor-inspection meeting on 18 January preceded the 20 January gathering; the article does not tie a state action to the gathering itself.

notes: The 20 January gathering is separate from the failed 18 January tripartite meeting. The report announces a possible strike in the coming days and planned black clothing beginning 24 January; neither plan is treated as executed. Keep the 800 affected workers separate from turnout.
open_questions: Did 50 or more people attend the 20 January gathering?
Was a direct demand made to the state, beyond asking the Labor Minister to help?
Did the announced strike occur before the end of January?
Was a state response tied to this specific action?

title: Redhac and journalists demand investigation at a Douala press conference
organizer: Réseau des défenseurs des droits de l’humain en Afrique centrale (Redhac); any formal co-organizer is not reported
participants_original: Journalists and some civil-society members; the record provides no attendance estimate.
threshold_50_evidence: The AFP video catalogue record describes journalists and a few civil-society members at a press conference but reports no total attendance; 50 or more is unverified.

start_date.summary: The INA record dates the first broadcast and its Douala shot list to 23 January 2023.

location.summary: The shot list identifies Redhac headquarters in Douala, Littoral Region.

organizer.summary: The item identifies Redhac and journalists as calling for truth; its footage summary identifies the Redhac executive director.

demands.summary: Speakers asked for a government investigation, public accountability for those responsible, and action from international bodies to press the Cameroonian government.

participants_original.summary: Journalists and some civil-society members are described at the press conference; no estimate is stated.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The catalogue record lists journalists and a few civil-society members but no attendance count.

state_target.summary: Statements direct demands to the Cameroonian government to investigate and account for the killing; some requests also call on international bodies to urge government action.

end_date.summary: The catalogue item gives no physical end time or final day.

protester_violence.summary: The catalogue record does not describe participant violence; the field remains unknown.

state_response.summary: AFP context says an investigation had already been announced, but no response to the 23 January press conference is established.

notes: This is a press conference in Douala, separate from the Yaoundé radio tribute on the same date. The sole opened item is an INA archival catalogue record for AFP video; the underlying footage was not viewed and no count appears in the record. Do not infer independent corroboration from its embedded AFP context text.
open_questions: Was this press conference open as a public assembly or limited to invited media?
Did authorities respond to this particular action?

title: Journalists pay tribute at Amplitude FM after Martinez Zogo’s killing
location: Amplitude FM headquarters, Elig Essono, Yaoundé
organizer: Journalists and members of the press community; formal organizer of the tribute is not established
participants_original: Opale Magazine search excerpt says about one hundred journalists; 237infos names journalists, politicians and taxi drivers but gives no count and has a conflicting date.
threshold_50_evidence: A search-only Opale Magazine excerpt describes about one hundred journalists at the tribute; the article body could not be retrieved. The count is attributed and no numeric range is derived. Actu Cameroun confirms the tribute but gives no count; 237infos adds a contradictory date and no number.

start_date.summary: Actu Cameroun dates the tribute to 23 January and Opale’s snippet does too; 237infos calls it “Monday 22 January,” an inconsistency retained rather than silently corrected.

location.summary: The body-accessed Actu report and Opale snippet place the tribute at Radio Amplitude FM in Yaoundé; 237infos also identifies the station but its date wording conflicts.

organizer.summary: The sources describe journalists paying tribute but do not establish a formal organizer; the Fedipresse minister meeting followed the tribute and is not assigned as its organizer.

demands.summary: The tribute itself is described as homage. Actu reports a later Fedipresse meeting with the Communication Minister to seek clarification, but the sources do not establish that demand as the tribute assembly’s demand.

participants_original.summary: Opale’s search excerpt says about one hundred journalists. 237infos names journalists, politicians and taxi drivers but supplies no number; its body was not retrieved.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The single approximate estimate of about one hundred comes from an unopenable Opale search result; the body-accessed Actu report gives no count, and 237infos has none.

state_target.summary: Actu places a demand for clarification at a later meeting with the Communication Minister, not clearly at the tribute itself; the tribute’s state target remains unresolved.

protester_violence.summary: The available material does not report participant violence; the field remains unknown.

state_response.summary: Actu says the government had promised an investigation, but does not tie that promise to the tribute as a response.

notes: Keep this tribute separate from the Redhac press conference in Douala, even though both concern Zogo and occurred on 23 January. The later minister meeting is not treated as the tribute’s demand or a separate public assembly. Count and exact date remain limited by search-only reports.
open_questions: Was the tribute assembly explicitly demanding state action?
Can the approximate attendance be verified in a body-read source?
Does the 237infos “Monday 22 January” wording reflect a different event or a date error?
Did the planned 25 January black-clothing or 26 January march actions occur?
Was the government’s announced investigation a direct response to the tribute?
